subject: Biology SL
title: Biology SL Paper 2 Section A Mock v2

questions.subject: Biology SL
questions.question: Researchers measured antibody responses after first and second exposure to the same antigen.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question: Compare the primary and secondary antibody responses shown in the table.
markscheme: The secondary response reaches a much higher peak antibody concentration than the primary response.
The secondary response reaches its peak sooner / has a shorter delay than the primary response.
markschemeJa: 二次応答は一次応答よりはるかに高い抗体濃度ピークに達する。
二次応答は一次応答より早くピークに達し、遅延が短い。
parts.modelAnswer: The secondary response is both faster and larger: it peaks earlier and reaches a much higher antibody concentration.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 二次応答は一次応答より速く、より高い抗体濃度に達します。

parts.label: (b)
parts.question: Calculate how many times greater the peak antibody concentration is in the secondary response than in the primary response.
markscheme: Peak ratio = 26 ÷ 8.
markschemeJa: ピーク濃度の比＝26÷8。
parts.modelAnswer: The peak is 26 ÷ 8 = 3.25 times greater in the secondary response.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 二次応答のピークは26÷8＝3.25倍です。

parts.label: (c)
parts.question: Explain the biological basis for the faster and larger secondary response.
markscheme: The first exposure activates antigen-specific lymphocytes and leads to formation of memory cells.
Memory cells persist after the primary response has declined.
On second exposure, memory cells rapidly undergo clonal expansion and differentiate into effector cells, producing a faster and larger specific response.
markschemeJa: 初回曝露で抗原特異的リンパ球が活性化され、記憶細胞が形成される。
記憶細胞は一次応答が低下した後も残る。
再曝露時に記憶細胞が速やかにクローン増殖・エフェクター細胞へ分化し、より速く大きな特異的応答を生じる。
parts.modelAnswer: The first exposure produces antigen-specific memory cells. These persist and, after a second exposure, rapidly divide and differentiate into effector cells, causing a faster and larger response.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 初回曝露で抗原特異的な記憶細胞が形成されます。再曝露時にはそれらが速やかに増殖・分化するため、より速く大きな応答が起こります。

parts.label: (d)
parts.question: Predict how the response would differ if the second exposure involved an unrelated antigen.
markscheme: Memory cells specific to the first antigen would not recognize the unrelated antigen.
The response would resemble a primary response, with a longer delay and lower initial antibody production until new antigen-specific clones are activated.
markschemeJa: 最初の抗原に特異的な記憶細胞は無関係な抗原を認識しない。
新しい抗原に特異的なクローンが活性化されるまで時間がかかるため、より長い遅延と低い初期抗体産生を示す一次応答に近くなる。
parts.modelAnswer: Memory cells are antigen-specific, so an unrelated antigen would not trigger the same rapid secondary response. The response would be more like a primary response.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 記憶細胞は抗原特異的なので、無関係な抗原では同じ速い二次応答は起こらず、一次応答に近い反応になります。

parts.label: (e)
parts.question: Evaluate the claim that a strong secondary antibody response means vaccination will always prevent infection.
markscheme: A rapid, strong secondary response can reduce pathogen growth and lower the risk or severity of disease.
Protection depends on factors such as how well vaccine antigens match the pathogen and how long effective memory persists.
Infection can still occur before the immune response controls the pathogen, so strong immune memory does not guarantee complete prevention of infection.
markschemeJa: 速く強い二次応答は病原体の増殖を抑え、感染症の発症リスクや重症度を下げることができる。
防御効果はワクチン抗原と病原体の一致度や、効果的な免疫記憶がどれだけ持続するかなどに依存する。
免疫応答が病原体を制御する前に感染自体は成立しうるため、強い免疫記憶が感染を完全に防ぐとは限らない。
parts.modelAnswer: A strong secondary response should improve protection and often reduce disease severity, but it does not guarantee that infection never occurs. Protection depends on antigen match, persistence of memory and how quickly the pathogen replicates relative to the immune response.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 強い二次応答は防御を高め重症化を抑えますが、感染そのものを必ず防ぐとは限りません。抗原の一致度、免疫記憶の持続、病原体の増殖速度などにも左右されます。

questions.subject: Biology SL
questions.question: Equal amounts of energy were supplied to equal masses of water and ethanol.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question: Calculate how many times greater the temperature increase of ethanol was than that of water.
markscheme: Temperature-rise ratio = 11.0 ÷ 4.5.
parts.modelAnswer: The ethanol temperature rise was 11.0 ÷ 4.5 ≈ 2.44 times the water temperature rise.
parts.modelAnswerJa: エタノールの温度上昇は水の約2.44倍です。

parts.label: (b)
parts.question: Explain why water shows the smaller temperature increase and why this property is biologically useful.
markscheme: Water molecules form extensive hydrogen bonds with each other.
A relatively large energy input is required to disrupt hydrogen-bond interactions, giving water a high specific heat capacity.
High specific heat capacity reduces rapid temperature changes in organisms and aquatic habitats, helping maintain stable conditions for enzyme-controlled reactions.
markschemeJa: 水分子どうしは多数の水素結合を形成する。
水素結合による相互作用を乱すには比較的大きなエネルギーが必要で、水は比熱容量が大きい。
高い比熱容量により生物体内や水域の急激な温度変化が抑えられ、酵素反応に適した安定した条件を保ちやすい。
parts.modelAnswer: Hydrogen bonding gives water a high specific heat capacity, so the same energy input produces a smaller temperature rise. This buffers organisms and aquatic environments against rapid temperature change.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 水は水素結合のため比熱容量が大きく、同じエネルギーを加えても温度上昇が小さくなります。この性質が生物体や水環境の急激な温度変化を抑えます。

stimulus.title: Heating equal masses of two liquids
stimulus.note: Both samples received the same energy input.

questions.subject: Biology SL
questions.question: Researchers measured glucose uptake by intestinal epithelial cells.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question: Calculate the percentage reduction in glucose uptake caused by the ATP-production inhibitor at an external glucose concentration of 8 mmol dm⁻³.

parts.label: (b)
parts.question: Explain why the inhibitor reduces glucose uptake and why uptake is not reduced to zero.
markscheme: ATP is required directly or indirectly for active transport mechanisms that maintain ion gradients used for glucose uptake.
Inhibiting ATP production weakens these gradients / active transport and reduces the rate of glucose uptake.
Some glucose can still enter by passive or facilitated diffusion, so uptake does not fall to zero.
markschemeJa: ATPはグルコース取り込みに利用されるイオン勾配を維持する能動輸送に直接または間接に必要である。
ATP産生を阻害すると勾配や能動輸送が弱まり、グルコース取り込み速度が低下する。
一部のグルコースは受動輸送や促進拡散でも入れるため、取り込みは0にはならない。
parts.modelAnswer: ATP supports active transport and the ion gradients that drive glucose uptake. Blocking ATP production reduces this transport, but passive or facilitated diffusion can still occur.
parts.modelAnswerJa: ATPは能動輸送とグルコース取り込みに使うイオン勾配を支えます。ATP産生を止めると取り込みは低下しますが、促進拡散などは残るため0にはなりません。

parts.label: (c)
parts.question: Explain how microvilli make intestinal epithelial cells better adapted for nutrient absorption.
markscheme: Microvilli increase the plasma-membrane surface area available for absorption.
The larger surface can contain more transport proteins, increasing the capacity or rate of nutrient uptake.
markschemeJa: 微絨毛は吸収に利用できる細胞膜表面積を増やす。
広い表面により多くの輸送タンパク質を配置でき、栄養吸収能力・速度が高まる。
parts.modelAnswer: Microvilli increase membrane surface area and allow more transport proteins, increasing nutrient absorption capacity.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 微絨毛は膜表面積を増やし、より多くの輸送タンパク質を配置できるため、栄養吸収能力が高まります。

stimulus.title: Glucose uptake by intestinal epithelial cells
stimulus.description: Uptake was measured with normal ATP production and after adding an inhibitor of ATP production.

questions.subject: Biology SL
questions.question: Plant cells were placed in solutions with different water potentials.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question: Identify the solution in which the mean cell length changed least from the initial length.

parts.label: (b)
parts.question: Explain why cells increase in length in the −0.2 MPa solution.
markscheme: The external solution has a higher (less negative) water potential than the cell contents.
Water enters the cells by osmosis, increasing cell volume/turgor and therefore mean cell length.
markschemeJa: 外液は細胞内より高い（負の程度が小さい）水ポテンシャルをもつ。
水が浸透によって細胞内へ入り、細胞体積・膨圧が増して平均細胞長が増える。
parts.modelAnswer: The −0.2 MPa solution has higher water potential, so water enters by osmosis and the cells become more turgid and longer.
parts.modelAnswerJa: −0.2 MPa溶液の方が水ポテンシャルが高いため、水が浸透して細胞内へ入り、膨圧が増して長くなります。

parts.label: (c)
parts.question: Predict the effect on a plant cell placed in a solution with a water potential much lower than −1.0 MPa.
markscheme: More water would leave the cell by osmosis, reducing cell volume and turgor.
The plasma membrane could pull away from the cell wall as the cell becomes plasmolysed.
markschemeJa: さらに多くの水が浸透によって細胞外へ出て、細胞体積と膨圧が低下する。
細胞が原形質分離し、細胞膜が細胞壁から離れる可能性がある。
parts.modelAnswer: More water would leave the cell, reducing turgor; sufficiently strong water loss could cause plasmolysis.
parts.modelAnswerJa: さらに水が細胞外へ出て膨圧が低下し、十分に強い脱水では原形質分離が起こりえます。

questions.subject: Biology SL
questions.question: Researchers measured the duration of stages in the cell cycle of actively dividing root-tip cells.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question: Calculate the percentage of the 20-hour cell cycle spent in S phase.
markscheme: S phase lasts 7 hours out of a 20-hour cell cycle.
Percentage in S phase = 7 ÷ 20 × 100 = 35%.
markschemeJa: S期は20時間の細胞周期のうち7時間である。
parts.modelAnswer: S phase occupies 7 ÷ 20 × 100 = 35% of the cell cycle.
parts.modelAnswerJa: S期は細胞周期の7÷20×100＝35%を占めます。

parts.label: (b)
parts.question: Explain why DNA replication must occur before mitosis.
markscheme: DNA must be replicated so that each chromosome consists of two sister chromatids before nuclear division.
Separation of sister chromatids during mitosis allows each daughter nucleus to receive a complete, genetically equivalent set of chromosomes.
markschemeJa: 核分裂前に各染色体が2本の姉妹染色分体になるよう、DNAを複製する必要がある。
有糸分裂で姉妹染色分体が分離することで、各娘核が完全で遺伝的に同等な染色体一式を受け取る。
parts.modelAnswer: DNA is copied before mitosis so each chromosome has two sister chromatids. Their separation gives each daughter nucleus a complete equivalent chromosome set.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 有糸分裂前にDNAを複製して各染色体を姉妹染色分体2本にし、それらを分離することで各娘核に完全で同等な染色体一式を渡します。

parts.label: (c)
parts.question: Explain how loss of normal cell-cycle control can contribute to tumour formation.
markscheme: If checkpoints or regulatory signals fail, cells with damage or inappropriate growth signals may continue through the cell cycle.
Repeated uncontrolled cell division can produce a mass of abnormal cells / a tumour.
markschemeJa: チェックポイントや調節シグナルが機能しないと、損傷した細胞や不適切な増殖シグナルをもつ細胞が細胞周期を進み続けることがある。
制御されない細胞分裂が繰り返されると、異常細胞の塊／腫瘍が形成されうる。
parts.modelAnswer: Failure of cell-cycle checkpoints can allow inappropriate division to continue, so repeated uncontrolled divisions can form a tumour.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 細胞周期のチェックポイントが失敗すると不適切な分裂が続き、制御されない分裂の繰り返しによって腫瘍が形成されることがあります。
